arxiv-2110-08317.title: Coverage Probability of Double-IRS Assisted Communication Systems
arxiv-2110-08317.creator: Anastasios Papazafeiropoulos, Pandelis Kourtessis, Symeon Chatzinotas, John M. Senior
arxiv-2110-08317.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anastasios Papazafeiropoulos, Pandelis Kourtessis, Symeon Chatzinotas, John M. Senior. In this paper, we focus on the coverage probability of a double-intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) assisted wireless network and study the impact of multiplicative beamforming gain and correlated Rayleigh fading. In particular, we obtain a novel closed-form expression of the coverage probability of a single-input single-output (SISO) system assisted by two large IRSs while being dependent on the corresponding arbitrary reflecting beamforming matrices (RBMs) and large-scale statistics in terms of correlation matrices.

arxiv-2111-08882.title: Search and Rescue in a Maze-like Environment with Ant and Dijkstra Algorithms Thanks: ICT Fund for Bio-Inspired Computing
arxiv-2111-08882.creator: Z. Husain, A. Al Zaabi, H. Hildmann, F. Saffre, D. Ruta, A. F. Isakovic
arxiv-2111-08882.description: Abstract With the growing reliability of modern Ad Hoc Networks, it is encouraging to analyze potential involvement of autonomous Ad Hoc agents in critical situations where human involvement could be perilous. One such critical scenario is the Search and Rescue effort in the event of a disaster where timely discovery and help deployment is of utmost importance.

arxiv-2204-01901.title: Thermodynamic properties of Schwarzschild black hole in non-commutative gauge theory of gravity
arxiv-2204-01901.creator: Abdellah Touati, and Slimane Zaim
arxiv-2204-01901.description: Abstract In this paper, we use the non-commutative (NC) gauge theory of gravity to investigate the thermodynamic properties of a deformed Schwarzschild Black Hole (SBH). Our results present a new scenario of black hole evaporation. As a first step, we describe the Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) mass, the Hawking temperature, and the entropy of NC SBH.

arxiv-2505-02146.title: QiMeng-Xpiler: Transcompiling Tensor Programs for Deep Learning Systems with a Neural-Symbolic Approach
arxiv-2505-02146.creator: Shouyang Dong, Yuanbo Wen, Jun Bi, Di Huang, Jiaming Guo, Jianxing Xu, Ruibai Xu, Xinkai Song, Yifan Hao, Ling Li, Xuehai Zhou, Tianshi Chen, Qi Guo, Yunji Chen §
arxiv-2505-02146.description: Abstract Heterogeneous deep learning systems (DLS) such as GPUs and ASICs have been widely deployed in industrial data centers, which requires to develop multiple low-level tensor programs for different platforms. An attractive solution to relieve the programming burden is to transcompile the legacy code of one platform to others.

arxiv-2506-22266.title: Symmetry oscillations sensitivity to SU(2)-symmetry breaking in quantum mixtures
arxiv-2506-22266.creator: S. Musolino, M. Albert, P. Vignolo, A. Minguzzi
arxiv-2506-22266.description: Abstract In one-dimensional bosonic quantum mixtures with SU(2)-symmetry breaking Hamiltonian, the dynamical evolution explores different particle exchange symmetry sectors. For the case of infinitely strong intra-species repulsion, the hallmark of such symmetry oscillations are time modulations of the momentum distribution [Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 183402 (2024)] , an observable routinely accessed in experiments with ultracold atoms.

arxiv-2601-05917.title: First-principles study of hydrogen diffusion in polycrystalline Nickel
arxiv-2601-05917.creator: Bhanuj Jain a, Alaa Olleak b, Junyan He b, Adarsh Chaurasia b, Davide Di Stefano a,
arxiv-2601-05917.description: Abstract Hydrogen embrittlement in metals is strongly governed by hydrogen diffusion and trapping, yet predicting these effects in polycrystalline systems remains challenging. This work introduces a multiscale modeling framework that links atomistic energetics to continuum-scale transport. Migration barriers for bulk and grain-boundary environments, obtained from first-principles calculations, are used in kinetic Monte Carlo simulations to compute anisotropic effective diffusivities.

arxiv-2601-22275.title: VMonarch: Efficient Video Diffusion Transformers with Structured Attention
arxiv-2601-22275.creator: Cheng Liang, Haoxian Chen, Liang Hou, Qi Fan, Gangshan Wu, Xin Tao, Limin Wang
arxiv-2601-22275.description: Abstract The quadratic complexity of the attention mechanism severely limits the context scalability of Video Diffusion Transformers (DiTs). We find that the highly sparse spatio-temporal attention patterns exhibited in Video DiTs can be naturally represented by the Monarch matrix. It is a class of structured matrices with flexible sparsity, enabling sub-quadratic attention via an alternating minimization algorithm.

europmc-pmc6185986.title: Sorafenib resistance in hepatocarcinoma: role of hypoxia-inducible factors.
europmc-pmc6185986.creator: Méndez-Blanco C, Fondevila F, García-Palomo A, González-Gallego J, Mauriz JL.
europmc-pmc6185986.description: Sorafenib, a multikinase inhibitor with antiproliferative, antiangiogenic, and proapoptotic properties, constitutes the only effective first-line drug approved for the treatment of advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite its capacity to increase survival in HCC...

pmc-11353067.title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Is Associated with Worsened Hospital Outcomes in Children Hospitalized with Asthma
pmc-11353067.creator: Jasmine Khatana, Aravind Thavamani, Krishna Kishore Umapathi, Senthilkumar Sankararaman, Aparna Roy, Ann-Marie Malby Schoos
pmc-11353067.description: Background: Studies have shown a bidirectional relationship between asthma and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). However, there is a paucity of national-level data evaluating the impact of OSA on hospital outcomes in pediatric hospitalizations for asthma. Methods: We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample and Kids Inpatient Database to include all pediatric hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of asthma between 2003–2016.

pmc-11454175.title: 6482 Knowledge and comfort in addressing eating disorders in people living with Type 1 Diabetes in an academic Endocrinology center
pmc-11454175.creator: Natalia Viera Felicino, David Lam
pmc-11454175.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Viera Felicino: None. Background: Eating disorders(ED) occur at twice the rate in people living with type 1 diabetes(PWT1D) compared to the general population. Early detection and prevention necessitate a high level of clinical suspicion, as the coexistence of ED and T1D is linked to compromised metabolic control, earlier onset of microvascular complications, elevated mortality rates and diminished quality of life.

pmc-11489300.title: CRYAB Promotes Colorectal Cancer Progression by Inhibiting Ferroptosis Through Blocking TRIM55-Mediated β-Catenin Ubiquitination and Degradation
pmc-11489300.creator: Haiyan Xia, Jingwen Chen, Wenbo Zhang, Ying Xu, Yongjun Nai, Xiaowei Wei
pmc-11489300.description: Backgroundα-Crystallin B (CRYAB) is a chaperone member of the HSPs family that protects proteins with which it interacts from degradation. This study aims to investigate the effect of CRYAB on the progression of colorectal cancer (CRC) and its underlying mechanism.MethodsCRYAB expression was evaluated in CRC tissues. Cell growth was tested by CCK-8 kit.

pmc-11682761.title: Recurrence rate of corneal squamous cell carcinoma in dogs undergoing superficial keratectomy surgery
pmc-11682761.creator: Helen Mather, Robin G Stanley
pmc-11682761.description: Background:Corneal squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is a rare neoplasm of dogs that can be treated with various modalities, principally by superficial keratectomy (SK) surgery. It is common to treat cSCC with multiple adjunctive therapies, but this may not always be practical for clinicians, clients, or patients.

pmc-12398506.title: Targeting pregnane X receptor with a potent agonist-based PROTAC to delay colon cancer relapse
pmc-12398506.creator: Lucile Bansard, Guillaume Laconde, Vanessa Delfosse, Tiphaine Huet, Margaux Ayeul, Emilie Rigal, Quentin Donati, Sabine Gerbal-Chaloin, Martine Daujat-Chavanieu, Luc Brunel, Baptiste Legrand, Alain Chavanieu, Anthony R Martin, Julie Pannequin, William Bourguet, Muriel Amblard, Jean Marc Pascussi
pmc-12398506.description: Tumor recurrence is frequently attributed to drug-tolerant cancer cells. We previously demonstrated that downregulation of the Pregnane X Receptor (PXR, NR1I2) reduces chemoresistance and prevents colorectal cancer recurrence in xenograft mouse models. However, there is currently a lack of clinically-suitable PXR antagonists.

pmc-12619458.title: Pleural and parenchymal radiological characteristics of tuberculous pleuritis and correlation with microbiological and molecular diagnostic yield
pmc-12619458.creator: Si Ling Young, Brian Lee Wei Chua, Qiao Li Tan, Carrie Kah-Lai Leong, Jane Jing Yi Wong, Ivana Gilcrist Chiew Sian Phua, Wen Ting Lim, Ken Junyang Goh
pmc-12619458.description: IntroductionTuberculous (TB) pleuritis is a common extrapulmonary manifestation of the disease, with significant healthcare burden and morbidity. While there is increasing use of computed tomography (CT) scans for evaluation of patients with suspected TB pleuritis, little is known regarding the correlation of CT findings and respiratory and pleural specimen microbiological yield.

pmc-12692608.title: Recommendations from Multi-Disciplinary Professionals for Survivor-Informed and Comprehensive Care for Human Trafficking Survivors
pmc-12692608.creator: Christina M Tsoi, Timothy B Smith, Elizabeth Cutrer-Párraga, Devan Clayton, Joshua M Marshall, Jamila Mastny, Alean Al-Krenawi
pmc-12692608.description: Background: Human trafficking affects millions of people worldwide with multiple adverse outcomes including psychopathology. Although research on human trafficking has become abundant in other academic disciplines (e.g., public health, criminology, social work), healthcare research specific to the mental health treatment of survivors remains limited.

pmc-13096711.title: How the Asthmatic Patients Handle During War?
pmc-13096711.creator: Anna Kovchun, Ayse Füsun Kalpaklioglu
pmc-13096711.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPsychological stress is increasingly recognized as an important modifier of asthma severity and control. However, objective clinical data on asthma outcomes during prolonged armed conflict remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate changes in anxiety, depression, lung function, and asthma control among patients with persistent asthma living in a frontline region of Ukraine during periods of differing military intensity, and to examine their associations with clinical parameters and access to controller therapy.MethodsThis prospective observational study included 49 adults with persistent asthma and

pmc-13145536.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1559 ATRIAL FIBRILLATION AND ISCHEMIC STROKE: PREVALENCE AND ASSOCIATED FACTORS FROM A RETROSPECTIVE STUDY
pmc-13145536.creator: Evi van Kempen, Wouter Elzinga, Tim Ten Cate, Anil Tuladhar
pmc-13145536.description: Background and aimsAtrial fibrillation (AF) is a common cause of ischemic stroke and a major global health burden. AF can be difficult to detect due to its often paroxysmal and asymptomatic occurrence. However, its detection is essential due to implications for anticoagulation therapy.

pmc-13148702.title: Cryptic marine gastropods in Hawai’i exhibit variable response to multidecadal in situ environmental changes
pmc-13148702.creator: McClaran Shirley, Amber Dawn Stubler
pmc-13148702.description: Natural history collections are a valuable tool to assess the effects of broad-scale and long-term environmental change on a diverse assemblage of species. Measurements from species that have been repeatedly collected over time within the same region provide an opportunity to infer morphological differences that have arisen as changes have occurred at the actual in situ rate of change.

pmc-13435666.title: A pilot study of nebulized 3D-cultured mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for the treatment of post-COVID-19 chronic cough
pmc-13435666.creator: Jihui Du, Yunong Wang, Hongyan Wang, Hongjie Zou, Chu Hua, Weihan Xie, Jiming Chen, Zhijiang Yu, Xilin Shen, Keke Wu, Cheng Zhang, Wenhao Wang, Bingbing Wu, Zhiyong Zhang
pmc-13435666.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionChronic cough, particularly prevalent in post-COVID condition (PCC, also known as long COVID), remains a significant medical challenge. Recently, extracellular vesicles (EVs) have gained significant attention for their therapeutic potential.MethodsIn this study, we explore the therapeutic effects of EVs derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) cultured in a 3D system (3D-EVs) in treating chronic cough, with a focus on post-COVID-19 patients.ResultsOur in vitro experiments demonstrated that 3D-EVs promote angiogenesis and cell migration, crucial processes in tissue repair and regeneration.
